next_authority.question: Which discrete ingredient of the prescribed-head lower boundary drives the persistent high-resolution spatial gap: half-cell head-gradient geometry, use of last-cell-center conductivity as boundary-face conductivity, or their interaction?

scientific_interpretation: The matched T16 runs finally separate the dominant scales cleanly: temporal error continues to decrease while the R512-R1024 spatial gap still increases.
The R512-R1024 bottom-flux RMSE grows from about 0.02233 cm/d at T4 to 0.02303 at T8 and 0.02340 at T16. The final increase is about 1.59 percent.

Temporal T8-T16 shifts are only about 0.00147 cm/d at R512 and 0.00180 at R1024, approximately 6.3 and 7.7 percent of the matched T16 spatial gap. Their descriptive orders rise to about 0.887 and 0.920.
Therefore unresolved temporal transaction error is no longer a plausible dominant explanation for the continuing R512-R1024 spatial difference.
The spatial-gap increments are shrinking, but no preregistered threshold permits declaring spatial stability and no continuum extrapolation is admitted.

The spatial difference remains confined to prescribed-head phases; HOLD differences are zero or machine-level. This is consistent with, but does not yet prove, a lower-boundary discretization mechanism.
Per the preregistered stop rule, brute-force T32 or R2048 extension is not the next default. Reference boundary/discretization mechanism diagnosis is required first.
